data.title: Philippine rescuers pull 41 more bodies from burned ferry
data.description: CORON, Philippines - The bodies of 41 victims of the worst Philippine ferry disaster in over a decade made their way through the blue waters of a resort area on Sunday, bound for a dock where forensic investigators awaited them.

data.title: Myanmar says UN envoy illegitimate ahead of credentials decision
data.description: YANGON - Myanmar's military-backed government said Sunday their UN ambassador -- loyal to ousted leader Aung San Suu Kyi -- is occupying the office illegitimately, as the organisation prepares to weigh his replacement.

data.title: China, Russia, India seek economic cooperation at BRICS
data.description: NEW DELHI - BRICS leaders including China, Russia and India entered a second day of talks in New Delhi on Sunday, discussing "inclusive global growth", after reaching rare agreement calling for calm in the Middle East.

data.title: Hospital apologises for cutting off toddler’s finger
data.description: The management of Loengnoktha Crown Prince Hospital has apologised after an assistant nurse accidentally cut off part of a toddler's right index finger while preparing the young patient for discharge, in the northeastern province of Yasothon.

data.title: One dead, 102 rescued from stricken ferry off Indonesia's Java
data.description: JAKARTA - One person was killed and more than 100 were rescued on Sunday after a ferry sailing between the Indonesian islands of Java and Borneo was hit by bad weather, rescue officials said.

data.title: Think-tank urges EC to submit Senate case to court
data.description: Thailand Development Research Institute (TDRI) president Somkiat Tangkitvanich has called on the Election Commission (EC) to submit the Senate election collusion case to the Supreme Court promptly, saying it would restore public confidence.

data.title: Ayutthaya nightclub raided, 20 customers fail drug tests
data.description: PHRA NAKHON SI AYUTTHAYA - Officials raided a popular nightclub in Uthai district early on Sunday after complaints it remained open after hours and customers were using illegal drugs. Twenty people tested positive for drug use.

data.title: Thailand faces its 2030 HIV target with youth infections still high
data.description: Thai youth aged 15-24 account for one in three new HIV infections, while stigma and unawareness of HIV status remain key barriers to the 2030 AIDS goal.

data.title: Donkoi Model turns royal guidance into jobs and modern textiles
data.description: The Donkoi Model, inspired by Princess Sirivannavari’s guidance, turns Sakon Nakhon weaving into modern fashion, jobs and Asian Games attire.

data.title: Forecast is for widespread heavy rain
data.description: Heavy to very heavy rain is forecast for 42 provinces and Bangkok throughout Sunday into Monday, with flash-flood, forest runoff and landslides warnings in vulnerable areas.

data.title: Poll respondents demand Israeli visitors obey Thai laws
data.description: An opinion survey found most respondents were aware of behavioural issues among some Israeli people in Thailand and support strict law enforcement as a solution.

data.title: Discover Phu Kradueng’s rare orchid in bloom deep in the forest
data.description: Phu Kradueng in Loei hides the rare Inthanon lady’s slipper orchid, Paphiopedilum villosum, which blooms each winter from December to February.

data.title: Sahasawat soars to PGA title
data.description: Sahasawat Ariyachatvakin claimed his first Thailand PGA Tour title, winning the Singha-SAT Nakhon Ratchasima 2026 on Friday.

data.title: Robinho strikes late as Buriram drop points
data.description: Robinho Junior's second-half goal denied defending champions Buriram United a home victory, while Port picked up their second successive win in the Thai League 1 on Friday night.

data.title: Govt denies role in US corn deal
data.description: The government on Saturday denied reports Commerce Minister Suphajee Suthumpun had signed an agreement to import one million tonnes of feed corn from the United States, saying the deal was between private companies.

data.title: Kop's back as Liverpool fans set to paint Bangkok red for massive run
data.description: Liverpool's Kop Run Bangkok 2026 will take place on Sunday at Plaza Court, Rajamangala National Stadium.

data.title: Panel inspects 'unauthorised' tourism project
data.description: A House committee monitoring the national budget inspected a tourism project in Samut Prakan on Saturday after the Royal Irrigation Department (RID) confirmed it had not authorised the construction plan.

data.title: Police rescue student after 1.78m baht call centre scam
data.description: Police have rescued a 22-year-old student who was manipulated by a call-centre gang into fabricating a story about winning a scholarship to study in the United States before transferring more than 1.78 million baht to the scammers.

data.title: CSD probes ex-monk's foundation over suspected laundering
data.description: The Crime Suppression Division (CSD) is investigating a foundation recently established by former monk Atichot Tanprasert amid concerns it may have been used to launder money.

data.title: More funds needed to fight tilapia infestation
data.description: The Ministry of Agriculture and Cooperatives may seek about 350 million baht in additional funds to control the spread of blackchin tilapia, as the presence of the invasive fish has now been reported in 21 provinces, a deputy government spokeswoman says.

data.title: Celine Dion makes long-awaited return to stage in Paris
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - Celine Dion wept tears of joy on Saturday as she fulfilled her dream of returning to the stage after years battling a rare neurological disorder, with a sell-out concert in Paris.

data.title: Israeli land network faces law
data.description: Justice Minister Pol Lt Gen Rutthaphon Naowarat says authorities are preparing legal action against a suspected network of Israeli nationals holding land in Pattaya, Chon Buri, as part of investigations into transnational crime.

data.title: Govt pushing Indonesia ties
data.description: MEDAN, Indonesia: Thailand is pushing for closer economic cooperation with Indonesia and Malaysia to expand markets, create jobs and raise incomes across its 14 southern provinces.

data.title: Mass protests await key rulings
data.description: Former leader of the People's Alliance for Democracy, Sondhi Limthongkul, is trying to pressure the government regarding the issue of "transnational grey capital". However, his campaign has not yet gained enough momentum to develop into a mass protest movement.

data.title: Chuan warns agencies on political interference
data.description: Chuan Leekpai, a Democrat Party list MP, on Saturday urged independent organisations to uphold integrity, impartiality and good governance in the face of political interference.

data.title: Intercity bus fares to rise from Tuesday
data.description: Intercity bus fares will rise by 3 satang per kilometre from Tuesday after diesel prices climbed to 39.84 baht a litre, the Department of Land Transport (DLT) said on Saturday.

data.title: Cambodia used Preah Vihear as base: Prapas
data.description: Thailand has evidence Cambodia used Preah Vihear Temple as a military base, Air Chief Marshal Prapas Sornchaidee, director of the Thailand-Cambodia Joint Information Centre (JIC), said on Saturday.

data.title: Venezuelans outside Caracas say capital not sharing blackout burden
data.description: SAN CRISTOBAL (VENEZUELA) - Josner Herrera is sick and tired of dealing with daily power cuts, especially when her part of western Venezuela produces a fair bit of electricity.

data.title: Fire at nursing home in Chile kills 16
data.description: SANTIAGO (CHILE) - A fire at a nursing home in Chile that had previously violated regulations has killed 16 elderly residents and left others hospitalized, authorities said Saturday.
